slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Inside: an angle formed by two chords that cross inside a circle is half the sum of the arcs intercepted by it and its vertical angle. On: an angle formed by a tangent and a chord at the point of tangency is half its intercepted arc. Outside: an angle formed by two secants, two tangents, or a secant and a tangent from an outside point is half the difference of the intercepted arcs.

Each is proved by drawing one chord to make a triangle and using the inscribed angle theorem with the exterior angle theorem.
